question: Who among the following is regarded as the father of modern Hindi literature and theatre?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatendu Harishchandra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatendu Harishchandra** (1850–1885) is regarded as the **father of modern Hindi literature and theatre**. He played a significant role in the development of Hindi prose and drama during the 19th century.
 
• Bharatendu Harishchandra is credited with pioneering modern Hindi writing, making significant contributions to **Hindi journalism, poetry, and drama**.
 
• He emphasized the **use of Hindi** as a medium for literature and communication, promoting its growth during the colonial era.
 
• His works include **dramas, essays, and poems** that reflect social issues, patriotism, and cultural revival. Some of his notable works include **"Vaidika Himsa-Himsa Na Bhavati," "Bharat Durdasha," and "Andher Nagari."**
 
• His efforts in promoting Hindi and creating literature that resonated with the common people earned him the title of "Bharatendu" (Moon of India).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jaishankar Prasad**:

 
 
• Jaishankar Prasad (1889–1937) was a prominent Hindi poet, novelist, and dramatist of the **Chhayavad era** of Hindi literature.
 
• He is best known for his **poetry collections** like "Kamayani" and plays such as "Skanda Gupta." His works focus on philosophical and spiritual themes.
 
• Although he was a significant literary figure, he is not regarded as the father of modern Hindi literature and theatre.
 
 
 
• **Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi**:
 
 
• Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi (1864–1938) was an influential Hindi writer and editor of the magazine **“Saraswati.”**
 
• He is credited with shaping modern Hindi prose and promoting the use of Hindi as a literary language.
 
• Despite his contributions, he is not considered the father of modern Hindi literature and theatre.
 
 
 
• **Premchand**:
 
 
• Premchand (1880–1936) is one of the most celebrated Hindi and Urdu writers known for his **realistic novels and short stories.**
 
• His notable works include "Godaan," "Nirmala," and "Sevasadan," which depict social issues and the struggles of the common man.
 
• While he is a prominent figure in Hindi literature, his contributions are distinct from Bharatendu Harishchandra’s pioneering works in modern Hindi theatre and literature.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Bharatendu Harishchandra:**
 
 
• He laid the foundation of **modern Hindi literature** and inspired generations of writers to use Hindi for literary expression.
 
• His works addressed **social issues, cultural revival, and patriotism**, which made him a central figure in the Hindi literary renaissance.
 
• His legacy continues to influence Hindi literature and theatre, and he is remembered as a visionary who shaped modern Hindi writing.
